passages.name: Что за шутка?
passages.text:
mrblue: We're a small community here — we don't love strangers much, and we value everyone minding their own business.
mrblue: We started calling each other by the colours our houses are painted. It began as a joke, then it stuck.
mrblue: By the way, we rented you this place because you're a redhead. Okay, only partly true. We really do like scientists here, especially professors and writers. And you're both a professor and a writer!

passages.text: msgreen: Yes — sometimes lost souls end up here, with nowhere else to go. And it seems like a pretty good place. I see you're already ginger and living in the orange house. I think you'll fit into our little community, if you want.

mrred: Many people underline it with their hair or clothes. You're free to do as you like — just try to respect others' space and don't pry.

mrblue: All right, relax — I know it's hard to get used to; I'm not fully used to it myself, though I've lived here more than ten years.

passages.name: Как ты тут оказался?
passages.text:
mrblue: As I said, I sailed here ten years ago. Red, Purple, and Orange were already living here.

mrblue: Circumstances meant I needed a quiet place. I had enough money, and someone introduced me to Red. He was just thinking of creating this little community for people who want a peaceful retirement.

mrblue: Literally a week later I was on this island. And here we are, ten years on.

mrblue: (thoughtfully) Yes — time flies here. Before you know it, a year or two will have passed.

links.name: Mister Orange? The one who lived in my house before?
links.link: Оранжевый? Тот кто раньше жил в моем доме?

passages.name: Расскажи мне об острове
passages.text:
mrblue: Well, it's a retirees' dream island. If you have enough money, you can live out your days here in comfort and joy. And none of the residents are simple folk — everyone has their quirks, their skeletons in the closet.

mrblue: (laughs) Though who doesn't, by retirement age?

links.name: But how did I end up here? I'm not retired.
links.link: Но как тогда здесь оказался я? Ведь я не на пенсии.

links.name: Thanks — I'd rather take a walk

passages.name: Мистер Красный всем тут владеет?
passages.text:
mrblue: Something like that. I'm not entirely sure how everything works here. But yes — this island belongs to him. And he built all the houses we live in. Well, not him personally — his companies.

mrblue: Except for Miss White's house — she insisted on a design of her own. And strangely, Red agreed.

passages.name: А не знаешь почему?
passages.text: mrblue: Even someone as talkative as me knows where the line is — and which questions not to ask.

passages.name: question
passages.text: mrblue: Maybe you have some questions? I can answer some of them.

links.name: How did you end up here?
Does Mister Red own everything here?

passages.text: mrblue: Maybe you'd like to know something else?

links.name: How did you end up here?

passages.name: Оранжевый? Тот кто раньше жил в моем доме?
passages.text:
mrblue: We were neighbours, so we became friends. He was the oldest among us and kept his beard ginger to the end. The nickname Mister Orange suited him perfectly.

mrblue: He loved to tell stories — but only about the distant past. Gradually his mind grew weaker, until he died this year. I miss him.

mrblue: But forgive me — I got carried away with memories. Would you like to know anything else?

links.name: How did you end up here?

passages.name: Но как тогда здесь оказался я? Ведь я не на пенсии.
passages.text: mrblue: You know, I ask myself the same question. Mister Red doesn't invite random people here. I think it's best to ask him — though I suspect he won't answer.

questions2green
passages.text:
msgreen: I still hope I'll get to read it.

msgreen: I'm sure you're curious about many things. We already know each other, and straight answers are a luxury on this island. But I can afford them. So ask away — don't be shy.

links.name: How do you like this island?

passages.name: Как вам этот остров?
passages.text:
msgreen: I like it here. I can live at peace with my beliefs — in the real world that wasn't always possible. And I still feel useful: if someone needs help with treatment, my opinion is valued.

msgreen: I also love the view from the lighthouse. If you haven't been there yet, you really should go!

links.name: How did you end up here?
Thanks — I'd rather go for a walk

passages.name: Как вы здесь оказались?
passages.text:
msgreen: Where to begin. I came here seven years ago at Red's invitation. I'm probably the only one who formally works here rather than renting a house.

msgreen: In those seven years I've grown used to this island. A beautiful place to die peacefully. I appreciate that.

msgreen: And in those seven years I've learned a lot about everyone who lives here. I'm a doctor — people tell doctors their secrets, if only to get a more accurate diagnosis. But medical ethics, you understand. I'm not a gossip.

msgreen: And I cared for Mister Orange. The previous Orange, I mean. The first death on the island. He was a good man and loved books too, especially plays. But I'm not ready to talk about that yet.

links.name: How do you like this island?
Thanks — I'd rather go for a walk

passages.name: Расскажите больше о себе
passages.text:
msgreen: I was a doctor all my life. And I still am one, though my patient list has shrunk considerably.

msgreen: I like helping people, and I'm good at it. I worked a lot with the elderly and helped them to the very end. So on this island my skills are especially valued.

msgreen: And as you've gathered, I love to read — especially good novels. Red once bought a whole shipping container of books to fill the library in my house when I complained that ordering books through him every time was too difficult.

How did you end up here?
Thanks — I'd rather go for a walk

mrred: Let's say I choose people who need quiet and calm. For different reasons — some want time alone, some like you need seclusion to write a book. And a solid sum in the bank. I'm a businessman, after all.

passages.name: Как так получилось что у тебя есть целый остров?
passages.text:
mrred: That one I'll tell you about. No secret there. About forty years ago I was looking for a quiet place for my old age. In retirement I wanted to live with my friends. At first I planned to build a whole village somewhere in the mountains.

mrred: But quite by chance, one of my business partners mentioned that some mad old man who'd made his money back in the Great Depression had gone bust and was selling his property — including this island.

mrred: It took me only a week to find a loan and make the first payment for this island. Then I gradually built all these houses and made it comfortable for retirement.

mrred: And here I am — though none of my friends lived to see the island finished. So I started renting out the houses. Over time I made new friends.

mrred: (laughs) Now I'm the mad old man who owns an island! Hope I don't go bankrupt.

mrpurple: Yes, I understand. I like the island. The atmosphere here is unlike anything else. It's quiet and calm, though troublemakers show up sometimes. But I don't think they'll stay long.

mrpurple: Now it's your turn to ask questions. Ask whatever interests you.

passages.name: Как ты оказался на острове?
passages.text:
mrpurple: I've been here twelve years already. A long time. Sometimes I visit the real world, but I'm more at ease with my thoughts and books.

mrpurple: Twelve years ago I sailed here as one of the first. Red and Orange were already living here. I became the third islander. It was quite an honour, actually.

mrpurple: At the time I was looking for a quiet place to retire — I'd just turned seventy and wanted to step back. I'd saved a fair amount, left something to my children, then transferred the rest to Red; since then I've been writing books and enjoying a well-earned rest.

mrpurple: Sometimes I check sports results — football, tennis. But less and less in recent years.

mrpurple: (laughs) Hard to follow a long championship when you're not sure you'll live to see the end. Though Green helps me a lot — she knows a great deal about old age.

links.name: What do you think of the others?

passages.name: Чем занимался раньше?
passages.text: mrpurple: You know the rules. No past. Here I'm a writer. What came before doesn't matter.

links.name: How did you end up on the island?
What do you think of the others?

passages.name: Что думаешь о других?
passages.text:
mrpurple: You're clever. You worked out how to ask. Yes — everyone here dislikes talking about themselves. But nobody minds picking apart someone else.

mrpurple: Where to begin… Red has lived here longest — fifteen years, I think. What he did before is a mystery to me. But he has a lot of money. Then came Orange, who died a couple of months ago. Thanks to Green, it all passed quietly.

mrpurple: I was third on the island. Then Blue sailed in. Around then colours replaced names, and we became Mister Red, Orange, Blue, and Purple.

mrpurple: Then Black arrived. All I know is he made his fortune on the internet — something in the grey zone, no details. He won't say more. Neither will I.

mrpurple: Then Green appeared — Red invited her personally when Orange's health declined. That was seven years ago. As far as I know, she's the only one who doesn't pay rent; money is paid to her. To her children, rather.

mrpurple: Yellow came three years ago. Around then the atmosphere on the island soured. She was always shutting people down when they talked about the past.

mrpurple: White arrived about a year ago. I know little about her — she's irritable and rarely talks to anyone. But she's the only one who got to build a house to her own design.

mrpurple: Seen her house? Very modern. Different from the others. I don't know what she paid Red for the privilege. But it was worth it — the sunset from her place is stunning!

mrpurple: Orange died a couple of months ago. And you appeared yesterday. I hope we learn more about you than we did about Yellow, and that you're more talkative than she is.

links.name: How did you end up on the island?

passages.name: Расскажи о Зеленой
passages.text:
mrpurple: Well… She's the local doctor, psychologist, herbalist — all at once. She knows a lot about plants and medicine, and how to brew a sleeping draught. Very useful in old age, you know.

mrpurple: I don't think you'll find anyone on the island who speaks ill of her. Except Yellow — she just dislikes Green's bluntness, and that she speaks openly about her past without fear.

mrpurple: But that's their business. I don't want to interfere. Though Yellow could be more polite.

links.name: What's wrong with Miss Yellow?
links.link: А что не так с Желтой?

links.name: What do you think of the others?

passages.name: А что не так с Желтой?
passages.text:
mrpurple: She's rude. And mean. Loves rules. Hard to talk to. I barely speak to her at all.

mrpurple: Though everyone on the island knows about her love of weapons. I'll bet a bottle of fifty-year-old whisky she used to trade in them and is just hiding here. She talks about it all too professionally.

mrpurple: But those are only my guesses. I dislike her because she's only sixty-one and thinks she's smarter than everyone. That's my personal opinion. I just wanted to warn you to be careful with her.

links.name: What do you think of the others?

passages.text:
mrred: It's not just for you — the others need to look you over, get acquainted, understand what you're about. We have a very cosy little world here and we're wary of outsiders.

mrred: That sounded a bit ominous, but it'll be fine — just come to the Bar tomorrow at three o'clock. See you tomorrow!

passages.text:

passages.name: Я пишу книгу
passages.text: mswhite: Yes, how interesting. I remember something like that — you said it when we met last time. Sorry I wasn't at my best; remind me what it's about.

links.name: It's a book based on my research

passages.name: Уже и сам не знаю
passages.text: mswhite: Yes, how interesting. I remember something like that — you said it when we met last time. Sorry I wasn't at my best; remind me what it's about.

links.name: It's a book based on my research

passages.name: Это книга - результат моих исследований
passages.text:
mswhite: Ah, science. Not really my thing.

mswhite: Though once I studied chemistry. I never finished university. It feels like another life, forty years ago.

passages.name: Я пишу роман
passages.text:
mswhite: That definitely interests me — I love books. I even wrote myself.

mswhite: Ten years of life wasted. I wrote two novels. The first was even published. But it was such a deafening flop. I still can't finish the second.

mswhite: And I've made peace with the idea that writing isn't for me.

passages.name: Расскажи мне больше об этом
passages.text: mswhite: (laughs sarcastically) What about the rule about not talking about the past? Or are you a rebel?

passages.name: Иногда правила можно и нарушить
passages.text:
mswhite: I was born a long time ago. Life wasn't sweet. Since childhood I found it hard to connect with peers and keep friends.

mswhite: But I finished school, then went to university. I wanted to study chemistry. I liked the idea of becoming the best experimenter in the USA. But study didn't agree with me — I couldn't stand the pressure.

mswhite: Then for several years I recovered; luckily I was never short of money. My mother left me a large inheritance, so I could do whatever I wanted.

mswhite: But figuring out what I wanted turned out to be very hard. Photography, acting, writing — at one point I even studied finance, but that didn't help much.

mswhite: (thoughtfully) Yes — that's how life went. From one problem to the next.

passages.name: Да, ты права, не стоит
passages.text: mswhite: How do you like the island? Have you got used to the isolation yet?

passages.name: Расскажи мне больше о тебе
passages.text: mswhite: (laughs sarcastically) What about the rule about not talking about the past? Or are you a rebel?

passages.name: question32
passages.text:
mswhite: I understand. I've lived here a year, but I still haven't figured it out for myself. Sometimes I love this place. Sometimes I want to escape. Sometimes I'm glad to be in such a cosy world, sometimes I want to return to the big world.

mswhite: Our talk gave me food for thought. Sorry — I want to be alone and take a walk. Thanks for the conversation. I hope you'll remember this as a proper introduction. And sorry I was rude last time. That happens with me.

mswhite: Have a good day.

//White leaves; map

passages.name: Спасибо что поделилась
passages.text:
mswhite: All right — let's not talk about the past. Sometimes it hurts to remember.

mswhite: How do you like the island? Have you got used to the isolation yet?

passages.text:
msyellow: Whatever it's like, it's in your honour. First and last time, so enjoy.
mrblack: Like walking in the forest? I've seen you there a couple of times.

links.name: Yes — it's peaceful in the forest
I think you've confused me with someone
links.link: Думаю ты меня с кем-то спутал

passages.name: Да, в лесу спокойно
passages.text:
mrblack: Yes. Especially when there aren't many people. You can explore other parts of the island too.

mrblack: That's my forest. And I like walking there alone.

msyellow: (laughs) Yes — Black was never known for his manners.

mrblack: I made my money on truth, not politeness. I say little, but I mean it.

links.name: I'll walk in that forest

mrblack: That's my forest. And I like walking there alone.

mrblack: I made my money on truth, not politeness. I say little, but I mean it.

Everyone falls silent.

msyellow: (smiling, offering her hand) Looks like another quiet one has joined our ranks.

passages.text:
msgreen: That's your right. I don't like them myself. They mean more work afterwards. Everyone here is quite elderly, after all.

mrpurple: We're still going strong!

msgreen: (laughs) Oh? Wasn't it you who didn't leave the house for three days with a headache last time?

mswhite: So that's where you disappeared after my party!

mrpurple: (embarrassed) Well, we don't have parties every day!

msgreen: How's your book coming along?

passages.name: Неплохо!
passages.text:
mswhite: I'm still waiting to read a draft!

mrpurple: Have you talked to our quiet ones yet? Seen Black and Yellow? It's like they communicate telepathically. They just stare at you in silence. Creepy.

msgreen: You just like to talk and their silence unsettles you. But it's perfectly normal not to want to chat all the time.

mrpurple: Maybe. But I think someone who keeps all their thoughts to themselves is more dangerous than the rest. Nobody knows what's on their mind.

mswhite: Wanting silence sometimes is perfectly normal. What do you think?

passages.text:
msgreen: Let everyone keep their own opinion.

mrpurple: What do you think of our council of elders — Red and Blue? Quite a pair!

mswhite: They're the ones who seem creepy to me. Sometimes I feel like one of them is watching me.

links.name: Why do you feel that way?

passages.name: Иногда помолчать с кем-то очень приятно
passages.text:
mrpurple: Let everyone keep their own opinion.

mrpurple: What do you think of our council of elders — Red and Blue? Quite a pair!

mswhite: They're the ones who seem creepy to me. Sometimes I feel like one of them is watching me.

links.name: Why do you feel that way?

passages.name: Почему тебе так кажется?
passages.text:
mswhite: It's just a feeling. Sometimes it washes over me. And I seem to run into both of them more than anyone else. And I love solitude.

mrpurple: You'll run into Red constantly on this island. After all, he runs everything — sometimes drops by to see if you need anything.

msgreen: He doesn't visit me that often. Probably afraid of doctors.

mswhite: Laugh at me if you want. But I'm telling you something's wrong here. And it frightens me.

mrpurple: If anyone frightens me, it's Yellow. I was walking this morning and met her at the lighthouse. The way she looked at me — as if I should apologise for being where she already was.

links.name: None of them scare me
links.link: Меня никто из них не пугает

links.name: Blue and Red scare me too
links.link: Меня тоже пугают Синий и Красный

passages.name: Меня никто из них не пугает
passages.text:
mswhite: Trust me — for now.

msgreen: Oh, stop frightening him. Everything's fine here. People are just different.

mrpurple: All right — we've probably tired you out. Will you go talk to someone else?

passages.name: Меня тоже пугает Черный
passages.text:
mrpurple: Exactly! Quite the silent type. Always keeping his own counsel.

msgreen: Oh, stop frightening him. Everything's fine here. People are just different.

mrpurple: All right — we've probably tired you out. Will you go talk to someone else?

passages.name: Меня тоже пугают Синий и Красный
passages.text:
mswhite: Exactly. A creepy pair. And they've lived here longest of all.

msgreen: Oh, stop frightening him. Everything's fine here. People are just different.

mrpurple: All right — we've probably tired you out. Will you go talk to someone else?

passages.name: Уже кое-что написал
passages.text:
mrblue: I bet the island is good for writing!

mrred: How do you like the island? Getting used to our way of life?

passages.name: Пока собираюсь с мыслями
passages.text:
mrblue: I think the island will be good for writing!

mrred: How do you like the island? Getting used to our way of life?

passages.name: Пока привыкаю
passages.text:
mrblue: I took a long time to adjust too. Orange helped me with that. We became friends quickly.

mrred: Yes — he was the life of the party. Knew how to make everyone comfortable. I'm sorry he died.

links.name: I'm sorry. Were you friends long?

passages.name: Очень нравится
passages.text:
mrblue: I'm envious! I took a very long time to adjust. Orange helped me with that. We became friends quickly.

mrred: Yes — he was the life of the party. Knew how to make everyone comfortable. I'm sorry he died.

links.name: I'm sorry. Were you friends long?

passages.name: Сочувствую. Вы давно дружили?
passages.text:
mrblue: (smiling) Well — who wants to go first?

mrred: You go.

mrblue: I met him on the island. Back then there was no rule about leaving the past behind, and we talked a lot. Remembered, shared.

mrblue: I've been here ten years. For nine and a half of those I had breakfast at Orange's house every morning. A wonderful start to the day. He understood people and knew how to listen.

mrblue: Green knows how to listen too. But she listens like a professional, extracting what she needs. Orange could share your feelings. We discussed ethics a lot — what was right and wrong in our pasts.

mrred: (interrupting) I knew him for fifty years. Even before the island. And he was always like that. Centre of attention, life of the party. I enjoyed talking to him, though sometimes he was very tiresome.

mrred: But we went through a lot together. And this island idea… it was partly his.

mrred: I miss him, but that's life. We'll all die someday. Maybe today.

mrblue: Well, I hope Green can delay that moment!

links.name: He sounds like a wonderful person!
You talk about him so much!
links.link: Вы так много о нем говорите!

passages.name: Кажется он был отличным человеком!
passages.text:
mrred: He certainly was!

mrred: Losing friends in old age is much harder. You won't make new ones.

mrblue: All right, enough. You're Orange now. The past should stay in the past.

mrred: The past should stay in the past.

links.name: Did you bury him on the island?

passages.name: Вы так много о нем говорите!
passages.text:
mrblue: He only died a month ago. No wonder we haven't got over it yet, right?

mrred: And losing friends in old age is much harder. You won't make new ones.

mrblue: All right, enough. You're Orange now. The past should stay in the past.

mrred: The past should stay in the past.

links.name: Did you bury him on the island?

passages.name: А как он умер?
passages.text:
mrred: Peacefully, in his sleep.

mrblue: As usual I came for breakfast, but he hadn't woken yet. That surprised me — he was always an early riser.

mrblue: First I tried to wake him, then I went inside and found him in bed. He was already dead.

mrblue: Honestly I still try to avoid going into your house. It feels like he's still lying there.

mrred: Then Green examined him. Her verdict was heart failure. Quiet and peaceful in his sleep.

links.name: Did you bury him on the island?

passages.name: Вы похоронили его на острове?
passages.text:
mrred: Yes, not far from the Beach. He loved walking there.

mrblue: It was a very strange ceremony. We all had to take turns digging the grave so we wouldn't have to call anyone from the real world.

mrred: Yes — I think it brought us closer.

passages.name: Сочувствую!
passages.text:
mrred: Thank you. All right. You probably don't want to listen to our memories and lamentations all evening.

mrblue: Yes — if you want silence, go to Black and Yellow. If you want conversation, try our talkative crowd on the pier.
